mission: ARC does theoretical alignment research aimed at methods that keep working as AI scales far beyond humans. Its current focus is 'mechanistic estimation': predicting a neural network's behaviour by analysing its weights instead of running it on many samples, which could help spot rare failures and anomalies.

key_work.title: Eliciting Latent Knowledge (ELK)
key_work.plain_summary: How do you get an AI to tell you what it actually knows, rather than what it predicts you want to hear? ARC's foundational problem statement.

key_work.title: Formalizing the presumption of independence (heuristic arguments)
key_work.plain_summary: Proposes a formal theory of 'heuristic arguments', informal-but-rigorous explanations of why a system behaves as it does.

key_work.title: Estimating the Probabilities of Rare Outputs in Language Models
key_work.plain_summary: Tests ways to estimate how often a model produces a rare bad output without having to observe it, which matters for catching catastrophic failures.

key_work.title: Competing with sampling
key_work.plain_summary: ARC's 2025 progress: aiming for estimation methods that beat simply sampling the model, using only mechanistic analysis.

key_work.title: Mechanistic estimation for wide random MLPs
key_work.plain_summary: A concrete case where analysing network weights predicts behaviour as well as or better than sampling.

key_work.title: ARC White-Box Estimation Challenge (with AIcrowd)
key_work.plain_summary: A public contest to improve ARC's algorithms for estimating the behaviour of random neural networks.

warnings.text: Powerful models could cause harm if they were trying to manipulate and deceive humans.
It is hard to understand or control what ML systems are 'trying' to do.
Alignment techniques may not keep pace as AI progress accelerates.

recommendations.text: Develop alignment methods that scale over many orders of magnitude, like pretraining and RL have.
Predict network behaviour mechanistically from weights, to handle out-of-distribution cases and detect anomalies.
Aim for intent alignment: AI that is genuinely trying to be helpful and honest.
